question: Actions of cholecystokinin include which one of the following?

options.opb: Secretion of pancreatic juice rich in enzymes

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin release" -> "stimulates gallbladder" -> "contraction of gall bladder" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin release" -> "stimulates pancreas" -> "secretion of pancreatic juice rich in enzymes" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin" -> "affects small intestine" -> "increases secretion of enterokinase" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin release" -> "stimulates gallbladder and pancreas" -> "contraction of gall bladder and secretion of pancreatic juice rich in enzymes" -> "increases secretion of enterokinase" -> "All" -> 85%
analysis: Cholecystokinin (CCK) is a well-studied gastrointestinal hormone with specific roles in the digestive system. It is known to cause the contraction of the gallbladder, which aids in the release of stored bile into the small intestine. Additionally, CCK stimulates the pancreas to secrete pancreatic juice that is rich in digestive enzymes, facilitating the breakdown of fats, proteins, and carbohydrates. These actions are well-supported by medical consensus and evidence. However, the role of CCK in the secretion of enterokinase, an enzyme involved in protein digestion, is not clearly established or supported by strong evidence in the medical literature. Therefore, while CCK has multiple functions, the most accurate and supported answer, considering the options provided, includes the well-documented effects on the gallbladder and pancreas but not necessarily on enterokinase secretion.
